guard: a startup kickoff remains owned until the Harness request is invoked, is dispatched once after pre-send idle or bridge recovery, and is never guessed back into the queue after an ambiguous post-dispatch close
why: The busy-startup cell first-reds on zero delivery and also counts marker occurrences so a double send fails. Recovery mutations run the production provider-disconnect fixture: a close before dispatch must still deliver once without an inbox wake, while a close after the fake records the request must stay at one attempt without claiming model execution. The hasDriveWork calls inside the error-retry timer and drive finally are structurally non-discriminable for pendingKickoff: the kickoff is cleared before the only run() that can increment consecutiveFailures and before every entry to that finally, and it is never re-armed. Mutating those sites could only grade unrelated inbox work or impossible state, so the reachable idle and bridge-recovery triggers are the ones mutated here. The second guard case holds a real soft-interrupt reply until the host logs that startup is awaiting it, then changes native status before acknowledging. The post-dispatch case emits an error before closing, so run rejects rather than returning normally from an empty event stream. The dnd case observes an automatic-inbox health receipt, releases the native busy turn, and expects deferred delivery without another wake. Provider-disconnect mutations select the startup-only group; its default smoke still runs both groups. The original steady-recovery assertions remain graded by provider-disconnect.json with --steady-only.
